title: Teacher training in the age of AI: Impact on AI Literacy and Teachers' Attitudes
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an online teacher professional development program can improve in-service teachers’ AI literacy, their current and intended use of AI, and their attitudes toward AI in educational settings. The authors frame the study around a practical problem: teachers are increasingly expected to understand and use generative AI, yet many lack systematic preparation and confidence.

The intervention was a four-week certificate course, “Artificial Intelligence in Everyday School and Classroom Practice,” delivered by the digital professional development platform fobizz. The course combined synchronous and asynchronous components, including kickoff webinars, self-paced modules, optional topical units on machine learning, ethics, inclusion, and data protection, live webinars/workshops, and a project phase in which participants created an AI-supported lesson plan. The study used a pre-post design with German in-service teachers from different school types, and measured AI literacy with a validated test and attitudes with a custom questionnaire.

Results showed significant gains in overall AI literacy and in most competency domains, along with stronger reported use of AI in daily life, lesson preparation, and assessment/grading. Teachers also reported feeling better prepared to integrate AI and expressed more positive views about AI’s educational potential, although some critical risk awareness also increased. The authors conclude that structured, hands-on professional development can support teachers’ AI readiness, but they also note that more specialized, longitudinal, and education-specific AI training and assessment tools are needed.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed pre-post intervention study, but it lacks a control group and relies on self-report for the attitude outcomes. Credibility is limited to a single-group design despite reasonable sample sizes and validated AI literacy measurement.
impact_tier_rationale: The intervention shows modest-to-large pre-post gains, especially in AI-use confidence and reported instructional use, with several effect sizes above 0.20. The impact is promising for a priority K-12 population, but the design limits causal strength and generalizability.

interventions.use_case: Online teacher professional development course on artificial intelligence and generative AI for in-service K-12 teachers, including webinars, self-paced modules, and an AI-supported lesson-planning project using a classroom AI assistant.

finding.finding_summary: Teachers' AI literacy improved significantly after the training program. Overall AI literacy increased from pre-test M=13.15 (SD=5.46) to post-test M=15.13 (SD=5.14) for n=291, with a small effect size (d=0.37, p<0.001). Ten of 14 competency domains also showed significant gains, including recognizing AI, AI's strengths and weaknesses, decision-making, ML steps, human role in AI, and ethics.
finding.measure: Validated AI literacy test (29 multiple-choice items + 1 sorting item) based on 14 AI literacy competencies

finding.finding_summary: The training was associated with greater reported use of AI for teacher workflow tasks and preparation. Teachers reported significantly higher agreement that they regularly use AI in daily life, use AI to create lessons and teaching materials, and use AI to support assessments/grading, with effects ranging from d=0.67 to d=1.32 across these items (n=436 for attitude assessment).
finding.measure: Self-reported AI use items for daily life, lesson/material creation, and assessment/grading

finding.finding_summary: Teachers' confidence and willingness to integrate AI increased substantially after the program. Agreement rose for imagining AI use in daily teaching practice (d=0.49) and for feeling well-prepared to integrate AI technologies into teaching (d=1.65), indicating stronger readiness and self-efficacy for adoption.
finding.measure: Self-reported readiness, imagined use, and preparedness to integrate AI into teaching

finding.finding_summary: Teachers became more positive about AI's educational potential, but critical concern also increased slightly. Agreement that AI in schools is more of a threat than an opportunity and that AI will replace teachers both rose modestly (d=0.42 and d=0.25), while belief that AI offers an opportunity to support students also increased (d=0.50), suggesting more nuanced risk-awareness alongside optimism.
finding.measure: Self-reported beliefs about AI's opportunities and risks in schools
